News / Cointelegraph / Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack

Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack Less than 1 min read

BTCUSD BNBUSD Binance said Thursday it had lifted all withdrawal suspensions related to its October hack, four weeks after an attack drained $6.3 billion in funds from the exchange in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. In an announcement, Binance said withdrawals had resumed across nearly all networks, with a small number remaining temporarily suspended due to maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack. The exchange’s network status page shows partial deposit and withdrawal suspensions for several cryptocurrencies. USDC withdrawals, for instance, remain suspended on Hedera and World Chain due to low hot wallet balances and on Sonic due to security issues. Binance warned users against phishing attempts, saying it would never request passwords or seed phrases or offer expedited withdrawals. The exchange also said customers could verify that their assets are backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 through its proof-of-reserves system. The Oct. 29 attack targeted Binance’s hot wallets across multiple blockchains, with blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributing the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Following the breach, Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses. Thursday’s announcement marks the end of a phased recovery process that began on Nov. 1, when Binance resumed Bitcoin BTCUSD withdrawals before gradually restoring services across other blockchain networks. News / GuruFocus / Mastercard Stocks Rise 1.94% as Payment Networks Gain in AI Selloff Rotation

Mastercard Stocks Rise 1.94% as Payment Networks Gain in AI Selloff Rotation Less than 1 min read

MA Mastercard MA shares rose 1.94% to $659.97 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, as investors moved out of AI hardware and into steadier earners. Visa gained 1.8% and American Express rose 1.2% on a day when the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% after dropping as much as 4.6% intraday. The rotation favored businesses tied to consumer spending volumes rather than data center budgets. Mastercard set a record close of $672.68 on November 4 after a 10% weekly run that followed its third-quarter report, TIKR reported at the time. Wednesday's close leaves shares 1.9% below that peak. The same session brought hotter October inflation data, with core PCE prices up 3.3% from a year earlier; higher prices tend to lift nominal card volumes, a mild tailwind for network revenue.

Mastercard's appeal in this tape is predictability: transaction fees with little capex, against an AI complex burning cash. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 98/100, with elite profitability and strong momentum, offset only by a more moderate balance sheet ranking. GF Value of $705.27 implies a 6.4% discount and a "fairly valued" label, so the shares are a quality refuge rather than a bargain. The next test is holiday spending data after Black Friday, which will show whether cross-border and domestic volumes keep supporting the premium.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Meta Platforms Stocks Jump 3.4% on Reported Amazon Talks Over Muse AI Agent

Meta Platforms Stocks Jump 3.4% on Reported Amazon Talks Over Muse AI Agent 1 min read

META AMZN Meta Platforms META shares jumped 3.4% to $609.89 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, after Fortune reported that Amazon is in talks that could let Meta's Muse AI agent back onto its marketplace. The reversal was sharp. Shares had dropped 3.74% to $567.75 earlier in the session, so the close marked a 7.4% swing off the low. Muse is a personal AI agent that books reservations and buys products for its users. Meta launched it in the U.S. in September, and more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set it up by October, according to TradingKey coverage of the talks. Amazon blocked the agent in September, citing its user agreements. Any deal would need sign-off from both chief executives, and both companies declined to comment. Andy Jassy has said Amazon is open to outside shopping agents if they deliver fair value in return.

A deal would give Muse access to the largest U.S. online store, the difference between an agent that recommends and one that completes purchases. That is the monetization path investors want after heavy AI spending, though terms could include fees or data-sharing that dilute the payoff. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 99/100, with elite profitability, a sturdy balance sheet and solid momentum. GF Value of $892.33 implies a 31.7% discount and a "significantly undervalued" label, suggesting the market still weighs Meta's capex more heavily than its earning power. The next test is a signed agreement; until then, Wednesday's rally rests on a report, not a contract.
